The instant petition has been filed for grant of the .
following substantive reliefs:
a) To issue necessary writ, order and direction to the respondents to pay compensation qua the portion of house and appurtenances thereto situated over Khasra No. 230, acquired portion denoted by Khasra No.230/1 now denoted by Khasra No.1839/230 in the latest revenue record, in accordance with law along with all statutory benefits provided under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
(b) To issue necessary direction and order to the respondents restraining them from causing any damage to the house, courtyard, stairs and breast wall situated over Khasra No.230 measuring 132 sq meters, more precisely over Khasra No.230/1 in Mukesh Prabhakar vs State Of H.P. sentences.text:
It is apt to reproduce paras 5 and 6 thereof, which read as under:-
5.
That the contents of para number 5 of the petition are admitted to be correct.

In this regard it is submitted that land comprised in Khasra No. 230/1, measuring 11 Sq.
Mtrs. was acquired for construction of National Highway-22 vide Award No.182/75, dated 30.05.1975 but during construction of road/National Highway-22 the said khasra number remained out of alignment of National Highway-22 and remained unused at the spot and due to which the .
house of petitioner existing on the said khasra number was not acquired at that relevant time.
6. That the contents of para number 6 of the petition are admitted to be correct.

However, in this regard it is submitted that as per the infrastructure map of road provided by the respondent No. 2 to the CALA/Land Acquisition Collector at the time of conducting survey for acquisition of land for construction of four lane the Khasra No. 1839/230, measuring 11 Sq. Mtrs. was out of ROW/alignment of four lane, as such the house existing on the said khasra number was not acquired for the construction of four lane.

However, as and when, the respondent No. 2 requests to acquire the house existing on Khasra No. 1839/230, measuring 11 sq. mts. or any additional portion of land of the petitioner the same will be done in accordance with law.

3 Now that the respondent-State has itself admitted that the house of the petitioner was not acquired at the relevant time, obviously the same cannot be utilized by the respondent- NHAI without paying due and admissible compensation to the petitioner in accordance with law.

4 In the given facts and circumstances, we deem it proper to direct the CALA/Land Acquisition Collector, Solan, to assess the portion of house of the petitioner and appurtenances thereto situated over Khasra No. 230 (acquired portion denoted by Khasra No.230/1 now denoted by Khasra No.1839/230) and pay .
compensation to him along with statutory benefits in accordance with law.
Ordered accordingly.
5 The petitioner is directed to hand over the peaceful and vacant possession of the premises in question as early as possible and in no event later than 21.1.2023.
However, before taking possession, tentative compensation amount be deposited by the respondent-NHAI with the CALA/Land Acquisition Collector, Solan.
6 The petition stands disposed of, in the aforesaid terms, so also the pending application(s), if any.

(Tarlok Singh Chauhan) Judge (Virender Singh) 11.1.2023 Judge (pankaj)
